current.text: His starting spot is not settled. Zion Williamson, Trey Murphy, Dejounte Murray and likely Yves Missi start, and the last spot is between Jeremiah Fears and Herb Jones.
A Pelicans beat reporter expects Jeremiah Fears to start over him.

The Pelicans have a crowded rotation of about eight players who could start, including Fears, Murray, Murphy, Zion, Saddiq Bey, Missi and Derik Queen, plus Bennedict Mathurin. This creates a minutes crunch.
The Pelicans have a new coach, Jamahl Mosley, who brings a defense-first identity.
The Pelicans are expected to be a weak team near the bottom of the West, at about 34 wins.
He belongs in the late rounds as a possible steal, though the expert is not a big fan of him.

durable.text: Steals are his main category. He gets many steals, some blocks and an occasional three.
He rarely shoots, so his points are low.
He is worth more in category leagues than in points leagues, because his value comes from category stats like steals.
His projected FG% is weak for his position.
He is not a true floor spacer, even though he shot about 42% from three in one past season.

note: Both Yahoo and ESPN give him 0 USD of value. He ranks 134 on Yahoo and 194 on ESPN, so he sits at the edge of our 144-player pool after costing 5 USD here last season. Steals are his one standout category (+1.8 z on 1.5 per game). His projected 40.7% FG on low volume makes him a fit for punt FG% builds that want steals, and a 1 USD late pick at most. Early in the season, check whether he wins the starting spot over Jeremiah Fears and whether his FG% climbs back from last season's 38.3%. If neither happens, he is a waiver player.
